notes.title: Lots of fixes showing up in Phénix today!
notes.content:
Bonjour, my fellow artists! 🍷🥖 

We’re releasing an update today that will mostly focus on a whole lot of minor fixes that we’ve been working on for a long time. It also includes the addition of a new brush that has been requested multiple times in our Discord community. See the full list below.

[h3]Additions[/h3]
[list]
[*] New brush! The Norlic brush, inspired by the request of one of our most active community members! This new brush allows for easier and more detailed blending of colours, available in Benjamin’s art supplies store!
[*] Automatic language selection on start-up.
[/list][h3]Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Rotating the sword pieces during the quest to get Shakespeare's skull should no longer result in a non-functional, square sword.
[*] Wiped away stuck bids.
[*] The colour of palettes should now be the same both while looking at them in the toolbox and while painting. You were not going crazy.
[*] Save file thumbnails will always appear.
[*] Fixed the rotation pivot of various interface elements.
[*] Fixed issues with flickering real-time light sources.
[*] The traversal UI no longer looks funky.
[*] Various buttons that sometimes stopped working will now always button properly.
[*] Selling a painting would sometimes result in all inputs ceasing to function, this is also now fixed.
[*] Players should no longer occasionally be whisked away into a boarded up house when loading a save file.
[*] The Australian sun has been tamed.
[*] The sound of the museum roof being lifted is now originating from the museum roof rather than at the centre of the world.
[*] The painting interface should now be a more suitable size for any canvas you decide to put on it.
[*] Passpartout would sometimes become afflicted with rapid onset glaucoma when rotating the canvas, causing his strokes to miss the target. He has been healed.
[*] The Teleshop interface should now always go away when you want it to.
[*] Increased the frame rate of some animations that would appear stuttery.
[*] Characters disconcertingly teleporting around the world should no longer be seen, even on ultra-wide monitors.
[*] Console input hints should no longer be visible on PC.
[*] The destroyed masterpiece now obeys the standard model of particle physics.
[*] The palette now contains all the colours of the palette when shown in the toolbox preview.
[*] Drawing on wallpaper does not completely screw up the wallpaper painting interface.
[*] When playing in ultra-wide resolutions all dialogue boxes should still be fully visible.
[*] The texture of the car that you draw on should no longer degrade in quality over time.
[*] It is now possible to change the quality settings of the game without discouraging customers from buying your art.
[*] Drawing on a golden silk canvas that has already been drawn on will no longer completely remove the old drawing.
[*] A hole in the ground into the infinite abyss has been filled.
[*] A lantern poking out through a wall is now properly aligned with the wall.
[*] The shop interface no longer pops out of existence. Well, it does, but you can’t see it happen anymore.
[*] The new canvas star icon should now act more predictably. 
[*] Anti-Aliasing should now be active when you expect it to be.
[*] The intro house painting experience is now less sad because at least there will always be paint applied to the canvas even if Passpartout’s hopes and dreams are shattered.
[*] Various performance improvements.
[*] Various localization mistakes were fixed.
[/list]
Happy painting!

notes.title: Passpartout 2 Turns One Year Old, Let’s Celebrate! ❤
notes.content:
Bonjour my fellow artists 🍷🥖

It is almost time for spring to come in Sweden 🌸I hope everyone is in good health and are doodling their hearts away!

Today marks the first anniversary of Passpartout 2(!!!!), and we are so grateful for the support of our nearly 80 000+ artists! To celebrate the 365 earth-spins Passpartout 2 is featured in the Daily Deal on Steam and is on sale with its deepest discount yet of 25%.

Now… To the most exciting stuff… Which we should probably have put on the top, you know, for engagement and stuff. Anyways…

This summer! Passpartout 2 is coming to Mobile & Tablets!
Finally you will be able to enjoy drawing on mobile and Tablet. Of course, you can draw with the touchscreen!

Here is a sneak peek of the mobile version we are currently making. Wow, look at that UI being all adapted and stuff!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/b8509fe6b9eef06b36a7f8babe729c0d048ccfbf.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/54dc7c6f8cf8d94404aeb7bdc26fac14b63b1d8f.jpg[/img]

We’ll open a mobile app pre-registration soon! Stay tuned for further announcements!


I am so hyped to finally get the mobile version out to all of you!

Happy painting,

It has been a while! I hope everyone is doing well in the freezing winter. Or, if it’s warm wherever you are, we are super jelly please send heat. 

Oh!
Today is Valentine's Day. So we have a sweet announcement to make.


We’re changing our relationship status from [b]“it’s complicated”[/b] to[b] “partner”[/b] as we can ecstatically announce we’re officially in a relationship with Wacom💛

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/e36518216b142b7ae0a48c2132126f28bd0ebef5.png[/img]

Passpartout 2 is now chilling inside the circuits of the [url=https://estore.wacom.com/en-us/wacom-one-pen-display.html]Wacom One[/url] as a free demo to try! Also, I must tease that we got some more exciting Passpartout related news coming. Teasing just to build suspense, you know, because I’m cheeky like that. Per usual we’ll announce that when ready. ❤️‍🔥

Papa//Mattias

notes.title: Patch 1.1.1
notes.content:
Hey! We wanted to publish a patch to follow up on our latest content update. This patch addresses:

- The studio looked a bit too well baked on the outside, so we turned down the heat somewhat.
- Adrienne should no longer improvise with lettering when making posters in polish
- Fixed an issue where a saboteur drew some extra lines on your fine art if you played on a low frame rate. This will retroactively fix paintings made since patch 1.0.2 and on (since october-ish).
- Someone (me) forgot to add the localization for the new things in Japanese. This has now been un-forgotten.

This is the final update for the year as we in the studio head into our blankets for the holidays. With that, thank you all for playing!

See you all next year!

notes.title: The Studio Update Now Live!
notes.content:
Bonjour my fellow artists! 

From the snowy landscapes I’m super stoked to announce our biggest update since the launch of the game. Say bonjour to:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/6b4d0eca3ac9f5cf4643756dddb458a8bd31c4b8.png[/img]

Sit down, grab a hot cup of tea as we explore what the update has to offer.

The studio is entirely remade. We wanted the studio to feel more special and like a historical part of Phénix. It also always felt a bit cramped to us (or what cheeky real estate agents would call “cozy”) so we made it larger to give you some breathing space.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/d037ae63d4cdd63db6d7bb12edf934e03e3fd7d1.png[/img]

We want the studio to feel like a home, like it belongs to you. So from this patch you can customize your studio by choosing your interior decoration style as well as flooring and wallpaper.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/3a2fc6064a4521b87df950a811309b51fea2b237.png[/img]

Now to the cool part. This is an art game after all. In the studio you’ll be able to draw your own wallpaper pattern - making the studio completely unique to you! Honestly can’t wait to see what wallpaper designs you’ll cook up!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/b3ecdefe9e2cc9cc71dabebf9a8574ba37e95538.png[/img]

A studio of this size surely needs a little companion, don’t you think? Well there seems to be a feline fellow roaming around town. That bed of yours does seem like a perfect cozy spot for a cat, doesn’t it?

Finally, we’ve partnered with POSCA to bring their pens into the world of Passpartout! The POSCA pen has always been the main inspiration for the Round Brush so now we’re finally able to call the round brush by its true name: The POSCA Round Tip.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/dd52d6ef5e4f3d1d1dc17c031d269c6300ce8323.png[/img]
You’ll also find the POSCA Chisel Tip in Benjamin’s store as a new tool as well as a few new canvases. Hope you’ll like it! ❤️

Let me know what you think of the update. Are there any decoration options you’d like to see in the future?

In the meantime I wish you all a very warm happy holidays. We’ll be back after the new year.

Cozy painting!
//Papa Mattias

notes.title: Now Steam Deck Verified, Tablet Support, and more!
notes.content:
Hello all! This is the resident code-wrangler speaking. With Passpartout 2 coming to switch soon (yay!), we've been working hard these past months to bring all improvements made to make it run well on the Switch console back to PC! This includes:
[list]
[*] Significantly improved loading times for new games
[*] Performance improvements, especially when running the game on Low/Medium settings
[*] Some 120 fixes, big and small!
[/list]
I noticed a mistake I made that affects the size of the application & patches that I needed to correct. This means this patch will be larger than you'd expect from a update without new content. Future patches (I hope) will only be large if they contain new content for y'all. ^^

We've also taken a deeper dive into tablet support. It's a bit tricky with all different brands and models around, and we've found there's almost always some steps required of the user to ensure it works correctly. To better the experience, we've changed the default settings of the game to be more brand agnostic, and added a new website accessible via the Settings menu that can act as a guide to setting up your particular model. We hope to update this site as we get more details from you users if there are any other steps needed for models out there.

Here's a highlight of fixes for this patch:
[list]
[*] You can no longer accidentally break quests that require characters to walk to specific locations by simultaneously doing another quests that asks the characters to be elsewhere.
[*] You can no longer interact with the invisible easel at the docks.
[*] When designing the flag for the community, now the correct characters are referenced in dialogue.
[*] Characters should no longer forget where their home is, even if it changes.
[*] Passpartout has now abandoned their ghostly self, and can no longer walk through certain objects & walls.
[*] If you hustle a painting to a customer and steal the painting as they pay, the customer will now forcibly take a refund.
[/list]
That's all from us this time!

notes.title: Save files are moving somewhere safer!
notes.content:
Hello all!

As some users have made us aware, currently the game can struggle to handle save files correctly. This has unfortunately lead to loss of save progress for users affected. To fix this, the save files are moving to another home!

[i]So what do I need to do?[/i]
Glad you asked! Most of the times, nothing! When you launch the game after this update it will attempt to copy your existing save files over to the new location. The old save files will also be kept safe & sound where you last left them, though the game won't use them anymore. Should the game fail to move the files for you, you can always move the files manually. To do so there are these following steps:

[olist]
[*] Navigate to Documents\Flamebait Games\Passpartout 2\
[*] Copy your steam-XXXXXXXXXXXXX folder
[*] Navigate to C:\Users\[YourUserName]\AppData\LocalLow\Flamebait Games\Passpartout 2
[*] Paste the folder in here
[*] The save files should now appear in the game!
[/olist]

There will be a bigger update coming soon-ish. We just didn't want to wait any longer with this particular issue.

Until next time!

notes.title: Minor Patch
notes.content:
Bonjour! First of all, a huge thank you for the lovely reception. Launching Passpartout 2 has gone beyond even our wildest expectations! <3 

Unfortunately we didn't manage to find and squish all the bugs before release. In this patch we're fixing some of the most critical ones - leading to the game locking itself, namely:
[list]
[*] Chatting to Margaret about Brianna's mission no longer leads to an eternal staring contest.
[*] Lancecour no longer soft-locks when playing in Korean.
[*] Added crash diagnostics to get better details of what may be causing a few users experiencing crashes when painting.
[/list]

We'll keep a close eye on all the bugs and issues you run into while playing, we're lurking all the forums and communities to gather a nice list of things to fix. Here's a few we've noted so far that we'll look into in the future:
[list]
[*] The hitbox on the buttons on the right side of the canvas take way more space than they should, leading to accidental clicks.
[*] One of the band members can sometimes get too excited and start playing their own music at the same time.
[*] Canvases in the overworld have a not-so-nice-looking stripe-y effect.
[*] Lancecour can go full exorcist with his head while sitting down. Creepy stuff.
[/list]

Again, huge thank you for your support! With this the development team will be checking out for Easter Holidays for a well deserved long weekend. Next week we'll be back and energized.

Happy painting!
/Papa Mattias

To make sure we select people who really want to play the closed beta we’re doing a second sign-up. You can sign up [url=https://www.passpartoutgame.com/closed-beta-test]HERE[/url]! 😊

If you miss out on the beta test, don't worry. The game will be fully released this spring! Oh my, that’s so soon!



Oh, and what a surprise, Passpartout 2 was awarded Best Visual Art at the Taipei Game Show!! We are extremely excited to have been chosen for this award out of more than 170 amazing games from all over the world.

We’d like to say 'Thank You!' to everyone in the community who has stuck with us making our weird little games.

notes.title: 📢 Exclusive Closed Beta Test + Sneak Peak of a New Area!
notes.content:
Bonjour et bonne année 🍷🥖


Today we have two exciting things to share. We’re planning an exclusive closed beta test. The idea is that we’ll randomly select from our Newsletter subscribers to get the opportunity to check out the latest version of the game‼️  *If you haven't already subscribed to our secret newsletter, sign up here > https://www.passpartoutgame.com. Our hope is that you’ll try to break the game in every way you can imagine and help let us know what mischievous things you accomplished so we can get rid of them before release. But if you just want to chill out in the game that’ll be totally fine as well ☕️


Secondly, I wanted to share some nice progress we’ve been making. It’s called Bull Street and its money-loving residents will hopefully find their way into your heart, or at least your wallet. These business people are on the lookout for clever art investments as well as needing an artist’s hand with various business ventures💰


The main reason I wanted to show off Bull Street is this awesomely endearing heavily trafficked road. JUST LOOK AT THE CUTE CARS GOING VROOM🚙🚗🚕! Uh, anyways, more info about the closed beta will come when we’re ready. The current plan is to run the Beta sometime in February, so stay tuned!

notes.title: No November News❓

notes.title: 🕵️ Words from a whistleblower: The truth about Flamebait!
notes.content:
People… I don’t have much time…My name is Kalle and I’ve been spending the last six months as an intern at Flamebait Games and I can tell you… while hacking this newsletter… that the Flamebait crew is a bunch of crazy wild cats and has no limits whatsoever... I’m telling you this because it needs to come out. Telling the truth is my new life goal. Prior to this, it wasn’t. I was a storyteller working with film, books and music - telling made-up stories all day long. Late in life, I found a way into the gaming industry and applied for an internship at Flamebait with the aim to expose them. To unveil their secrets. Because it has to be something, right? And wow… I mean WOW😲! 

 

First of all, as an intern, you expect to get simple tasks like making coffee, sorting papers, and maybe hosting an Instagram account for a week or two. Flamebait… made me work! I’ve been forced to make character designs, and quests and write narratives and dialogues from day one. I hosted game tests and analyzed the results. They are actually listening to what I have to say and are, at this very moment, implementing my designs into Passpartout 2. I am an intern, for christ's sake! Yes, I’ve been writing professionally for 20 years but still: an intern! Why don’t they want my coffee ☕️?


 
I have broken the game several times - no punishment! I have on one occasion accidentally knocked a glass of water out of the lead artist's hand without retaliation. They are suspiciously kind. Or simply decent human beings🤔.

 

Anyways - I guess you knew this already. What a lousy whistleblower I would be if I didn't disclose anything new. So I made a screen recording of me testing out our new tools🎨, making a self-portrait exclusively for you. I don't know what kind of trouble I will endure for unveiling this. If they choose the Flamebait way… they probably will offer me a job or something…
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/9711a25f2a31805b7c95672c76f9b21fe6a30cf6.gif[/img]


On a more serious note, I would like to say that I am super proud of being part of this game and I hope that my involvement added a nice flavour to Passpartout 2. You’ll soon be able to see for yourselves.

 
Yours sincerely

Kalle Carmback, Game Design intern.

notes.title: 🎨When Can I Play The Game??? SOOON!!
notes.content:
Hello fellow artists🥖🍷


So many of you have asked “When can I play the game?”, “When’s the Beta?”, etc… And we’ve channeled our inner politicians for so long by giving the vaguest of answers. By the way, if you elect me I’ll make sure every citizen gets one free baguette per day. Anyways, today we’re politicians no more! (Unless you ask other questions we’re not ready to answer). Very soon you’ll all be able to get your hands on a slice of Passpartout 2 as we’re taking part in the Steam Next Fest June 2022 🎉


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/a57016ee5bafe0727c228627f57c81e97a19884a.png[/img]


The demo will be available to play on Steam June 13th-20th! We’ve been working hard with trimming brushes, mixing paint and wiggling them puppets and we hope you’ll have a blast with it! It’ll be time exclusive so don’t miss this chance to check out the game and give us all the juicy feedback of what you love and hate (or maybe what you’re just luke-warm to). 


If you can’t wait and just want to spend the coming days leading up to the demo staring at an image of the game in pure hype and suspense I got ya covered! Disclaimer, don’t stare for too long periods at a time, don’t forget to blink and remember to eat, sleep and hydrate.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/9ccbb1239df9cdab36e8e21aa44bfa1235ef74a0.png[/img]


We’ll send out a little boop once the demo goes live so you won’t miss it. But to be safe you should mark June 13th down in your little calendar or on your fridge or wherever you mark stuff down you ought to remember!


Until then, keep being as awesome as always❤️


//Mattias

notes.title: Woah❤️ 20k is a Big Number! Thank You!
notes.content:
Bonjour fellow artists🍾🍷

We recently reached a milestone of 20 000 wishlists for Passpartout 2! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/26cb66b6ca1798da8bfef3c522d91274b52f8431.png[/img]

We’re grateful and impressed by your wishlisting abilities. It’s amazing to see so many people excited to pick up the paintbrush again. Speaking of brushes we recently did some improvements to the watercolor brush I’d love to share with you.


Now I consider myself a mediocre artist at best, so for me it’s important that the brushes in Passpartout 2 help me make beautiful art. So far my favorite is the watercolor brush. It leaves behind this lovely texture that chaotically builds shapes that I can add to, helping me create some pretty sweet art. I especially like using it for drawing water or fire, but I’m sure the creative minds out there can find many more uses for it! I mean, the masterpieces you made with the barebones tools of Passpartout 1 is mind blowing so I can only imagine what you’ll cook up with this!


Here’s a little time lapse of me using the watercolor and some other tools to draw a tiny boat on the ocean, minutes before getting hugged by a big-boy octopus. 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/dbc200ea9902866e90d46d54c50459be060411a8.gif[/img]


Now it’s time to go back to the development dungeon. Thank you for tuning in and stay awesome! 




/Mattias

notes.title: 👀 First Look at the Painting in Passpartout 2!
notes.content:
Heya! Mattias here, Game Director for Passpartout 2🍷🥖

 I hope you had an amazing Winter Holiday and a great New Year! It’s been time consuming but we’re finally ready to share some of the tools we’ve got cooking! 


Drawing is obviously important in Passpartout so I’m happy we’ve been able to take a ton of time to make them feel great. When designing the tools we wanted something that felt playful, was easy to use and that inspired you to create. The results? Well, you can check out the tools in action below!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581837/44f2c85da66cc304dbf451ce9e2db9e51b87ccf2.gif[/img]


Each tool has its own texture and feel and by combining them you can create some really cool stuff! The painting experience is kept in the spirit of Passpartout by keeping it easy to use. You're able to change among the many tools and change size or color. We leave layers, filters and other advanced stuff to the painting softwares out there to keep the game lighthearted and fun!


Let us know what you think in the [url=https://discord.com/invite/flamebaitgames]Discord[/url]! Are there any tools you want to see in the game?


/Mattias
